title: The front door isn't locked
prompt: Painterly dark-fantasy illustration in the style of a cinematic tabletop RPG book spread: wide 16:9 landscape composition, dramatic lighting with warm ember-orange highlights against cold ice-blue shadows, rich texture, a clear focal point. No text, no captions, no speech bubbles, no logos, no watermark. Scene: the great front gate of Frostfall Fortress, a grim old stone outpost above a ravine of ice, at dusk, snow in the air. Ulrick: a broad-shouldered human paladin with short swept-back dark brown hair and a full dark beard, wearing heavy dark plate armour with bronze-orange pauldrons and a long white cloth tabard over the armour; he is loaded down like a siege engine: a portable battering ram over one shoulder, a spare ram under his arm, and barrels of oil and tar strapped to his back, ready to blow the place apart. Beside him, Durzo: a lean half-elf rogue with swept-back silver-white hair and pointed ears, in fitted red-and-black leather armour; he has simply pushed the huge door with one finger and it is swinging open with a creak, unlocked. He looks back at Ulrick, deadpan. Ulrick's face: disappointment, and a hopeful look at his barrels. Comedy played straight, cold blue dusk with warm torchlight from inside the doorway.
